{{Short description|Math equation}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''spheroidal wave equation''' is given by

:<math>(1-t^2)\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} -2(b+1) t\, \frac{d y}{dt} + (c - 4qt^2) \, y=0</math>

It is a generalization of the [[Mathieu differential equation]].<ref>see Abramowitz and Stegun, [http://people.math.sfu.ca/~cbm/aands/page_722.htm page 722]</ref>
If <math>y(t)</math> is a solution to this equation and we define <math>S(t):=(1-t^2)^{b/2}y(t)</math>, then <math>S(t)</math> is a [[prolate spheroidal wave function]] in the sense that it satisfies the equation<ref>see Bateman, [https://archive.org/details/partialdifferent033549mbp/page/n469, page 442]</ref>

:<math>(1-t^2)\frac{d^2S}{dt^2} -2 t\, \frac{d S}{dt} + (c - 4q + b + b^2 + 4q(1-t^2) - \frac{b^2}{1-t^2} ) \, S=0</math>
